# diagnose sys ha reset-uptime        <-- run on the primary to force a failover (override disabled)
# diagnose sys ha dump-by vcluster
...
FGVMxx92:...uptime/reset_cnt=7814/0    <-- HA uptime 7814 s higher than the peer
FGVMxx93:...uptime/reset_cnt=0/1       <-- 0 = member with the lowest HA uptime; reset_cnt = times its HA uptime was reset
cap: HA uptime difference and reset count used in the election
g: With override disabled HA uptime is compared before priority, and only a difference of at least five minutes counts. reset-uptime sets the HA uptime (not system uptime) to 0; a failed monitored interface or a reboot does the same.

C    *> 100.65.0.0/24 is directly connected, port2

cap: Routing database: selected/FIB flags (Fortinet sample question 15; codes line as in lab p51)
g: Both default routes carry *>, so both are in the routing table; the port2 route is preferred because its priority (1) is lower. Neither is inactive and both have distance 10. A standby (higher-distance) route would appear here without *> and not appear in routing-table all.
